# Pi adapter for the reviewed pstack source

The behavior source is the immutable `vendor/upstream/0.15.32/pstack/` Markdown snapshot at `99b609a72323b70204eab407c622f436e858e112`. The generated supported Skill/playbook entrypoints retain its instructions, with platform adaptations in a separate prelude. Do not summarize away upstream rules. The eleven core workflows retain critical-rule mappings; other generated entrypoints preserve the latest source without claiming full behavioral audit.

Apply user instructions and repository authority first. Apply the pinned upstream decision rules next, subject only to the explicit overrides below. Never run a Cursor command literally or assume a missing capability completed. Read referenced source Markdown through `pstack_skill` with `upstream/skills/<skill>/...` resource IDs; consume every page. Original relative links resolve within that snapshot. ## Platform substitutions

- Pi Skill frontmatter uses the resource directory name in lowercase kebab case. Upstream 0.15.32 already uses `poteto-mode`; bodies and manual invocation flags remain intact.

- Task and cloud workers map to `pstack_agents` and `pstack_workflow` Pi AgentSessions. The parent keeps playbook ownership. Parallel writers require separate Git worktrees; integrated delivery requires an explicit integrator followed by verification of the combined artifact. These are local processes, not cloud VMs.
- Map upstream reasoning effort to explicit Pi `thinkingLevel` and pick an available `provider/model` for speed. The adapter does not rewrite Cursor `-fast` aliases or silently switch model families. Unsupported effort settings fail in the model router.
- Resolve model roles through `~/.pi/agent/pstack-native/models.json` (or PSTACK_NATIVE_HOME) and available Pi provider/model selectors. For panels name every seat explicitly. Use `pstack_semantics` panel preflight; no silent provider/model fallback. Unavailable models block the affected seat and must be reported. This deliberately replaces upstream family-default fallback.
- `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc`, `.cursor/skills` and Cursor's plugin paths map to Pi configuration and the bundled snapshot. They are not files the Pi worker should create in a user's repository.
- Custom Mode maps to sticky `/poteto-mode`. `/loop` maps to `/pstack-loop`, which needs an active Pi host. Cloud-root hourly execution and exact delivery across a crash are unavailable; report this limitation before promising unattended audit coverage.
- Use a named available CLI/UI driver for real-surface proof. If no driver can reach the surface, return BLOCKED or inconclusive with the exact reason. Unit tests, fake providers, a worker's report or CI alone cannot replace the live lane.

## Explicit policy deviations

- For initial or major autopilot changes, require a full swarm. For a minor fix, rebase or conflict resolution, one fresh independent follow-up reviewer can replace a new full swarm only when a clean initial/major round is supplied. Fresh gates and live proof still run at the current head/base. A follow-up without that prior full round is blocked.
- Any head OR base change invalidates native verification and every round receipt, even when stable patch IDs match. Re-run lanes on the current exact pair. Upstream's build-noise/patch-ID reuse exception is intentionally disabled; the stricter native ledger policy remains in force.
- Read-only reviewer/verifier sessions inspect confined source and evidence; they cannot run shell commands. Deterministic commands run in the native verification runner or an authorized writable lane. A separate actor inspects the receipts; a writer cannot countersign its own work.
- The native arena template evaluates each candidate with separate judge nodes rather than one cross-judge that sees all candidates. Use an explicit DAG for the upstream single-cross-judge choreography. Native specialized templates are mechanisms, not automatic completion of a named upstream playbook.
- Native swarm templates cover partition and best-of race. Mixed/first-pass/rank-all require an explicit DAG and declared selection policy; do not silently relabel best-of as first-pass.
- The native autopilot templates prepare local DAG artifacts. Full owner lifecycle, early ready PR, decisions.tsv/children.tsv, periodic audit, rebase discipline, root countersigns and stop propagation remain obligations of the coordinator. The stack template is not a delivered remote PR stack; use stack-plan/stack-open with correct parent worktrees.
- Babysit stops before merge, even when checks are green. Opening a PR does not start a babysit. An explicitly assigned full-autonomy owner may begin its assigned loop after its code-ready report; other agents finish their phase or stack before the handoff. Autopilot-stack stops before shipping. Full-autopilot still needs the operator's go; operator-reserved items never merge automatically. Use `pstack_semantics` round checks before a clean verdict, then native Frontier, ledger and authorization checks for any shipping operation. The round check neither attests the truth of supplied receipts nor authorizes a remote action.

## Unsupported operations

`Cursor-private-PR-provenance`, `Cursor-watch-READY`, `Cursor-cleanup-plugin` and `Bugbot-pass-dismissal` are unsupported. Querying one through `pstack_semantics` fails with an explicit error. GitHub/Origin state and native watch states are usable alternatives only within their own evidence boundary, not proof that a Cursor operation ran. Private provenance, queue verdicts and pass-based dismissal cannot be inferred from green CI. Do not mark a workflow complete when one of its required operations is unavailable.

## Evidence boundary

`SEMANTICS.json` records critical-rule mappings, exact source ranges, deviations, test references and review fingerprints. Inventory counts, mapping coverage, deterministic receipt tests, fake-provider Pi lifecycle tests and real-model runs are separate evidence levels. No mapping asserts complete chat/model equivalence. Updating a fingerprint records review work; it is not semantic approval. Advancing a source pin does not grant semantic approval; that still requires explicit maintainer sign-off. The active source is 0.15.32; its implementation audit, maintainer semantic sign-off and real-model evidence remain separate fields in SEMANTICS.json. The previous 0.15.17 snapshot is retained for provenance.

## Pinned upstream instructions

Source: cursor/plugins@99b609a72323b70204eab407c622f436e858e112, pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/hillclimb.md. The following body is retained verbatim.

## Steps

### Hillclimb

**You own the metric and the experiment's integrity. Supervise and review. Delegate the attempts.** For sustained, iterative improvement of one measurable thing against a target. A one-off fix is Bug fix or Perf issue. This is the loop.

Core discipline: one change, one measurement, keep or revert. Never stack untested changes, and never claim a win from code inspection (the **prove-it-works** principle skill).

1. Ground the workload and architecture before choosing the metric. Run the **how** skill over the target, name the realistic workload dimensions that can move the result (data size, history, state, concurrency), and select a case that reproduces the user's complaint. If no case reproduces it, fix the repro instead of hillclimbing. Then fix one metric, the direction that counts as better, and a checkable stop predicate that pairs a target with a floor on attempts so a lucky early win can't end the run (the example "at least 50% better than baseline and at least 10 iterations" is this shape). Use the user's numbers when given, otherwise agree them.
2. Build the measurement harness, prove its sensitivity, then freeze it (the **build-the-lever** principle skill). Run contrasting realistic workloads and confirm the target case reproduces the symptom while easier cases separate as expected. If the harness cannot distinguish them, revise the workload or metric. Vet the harness with the **benchmark-checklist** skill before you freeze it, and make it print its error count and a count of the work done. Once frozen, one repeatable command emits the metric, sampled enough to clear the noise (median of N, not a single run). Record the baseline metric and a green run of the regression gate (the tests that must keep passing) before any change.
3. Open the decision log via the **show-me-your-work** skill. A `decision.tsv`, one row per attempt: id, hypothesis, change, before, after, delta, tests, verdict (kept or reverted), note. Read it before each attempt. Keep it out of the tree (gitignored).
4. Ground each hypothesis in the architecture model from step 1, so it names a specific mechanism ("defer X off the boot path because it blocks first paint"), not "try memoizing something". For a perf metric, order hypotheses by the performance mantras in step 2 of the Perf issue playbook (`playbooks/perf-issue.md`). Borrow only their order, not that step's stop rule.
5. Loop, one hypothesis per iteration:
   - Hand the change to a subagent using your configured hillclimb model (default `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast`) with a tight scope. Pick each subagent's reasoning level and fast or standard speed for the job, per the Subagents section. Supervise and review the diff rather than typing it (the **guard-the-context-window** principle skill). When several independent hypotheses are live, fan them to parallel subagents, each in its own worktree (the **separate-before-serializing-shared-state** principle skill).
   - Measure before and after with the frozen harness, and run the regression gate.
   - Accept only when the metric moves past noise and the gate stays green. Otherwise revert the change in full. A tweak that "might help" is not kept.
   - One commit per accepted fix, staging only the files you changed (`git add <files>`, never `-A`). Log the row either way, kept or reverted.
   Each iteration ends in a check before the next begins (the **sequence-verifiable-units** principle skill). If the run is unattended, borrow only the wake mechanism from the Autonomous run playbook (`playbooks/autonomous-run.md`), not its stop rule.
6. Push past the first plateau. On a stall, several rejects in a row, pivot category, combine near-misses, re-read the source, or try something more radical before concluding the hill is climbed. Correctness and simplicity outrank the number. Revert a win that breaks behavior, and keep a simplification that holds the number (the **laziness-protocol** principle skill).
7. Stop when the predicate is met, or when the remaining ideas are marginal and not worth their cost. Don't relax the predicate to meet it, and don't quit while cheap untried hypotheses remain. If you are stuck, surface it instead of spinning.
8. Run **Opening a PR** with the accepted commits stacked in the order they landed.

**Reply:** the metric and target, baseline to final with the percent delta, iterations run (kept vs reverted), each accepted fix on one line, the `decision.tsv` path, and the best idea you would try next if pushed further.


## Pi execution tools

Use `pstack_agents` for one child and `pstack_workflow` / `pstack_graph` for an explicit DAG. Roles are `architect`, `worker`, `reviewer`, `verifier`, `synthesizer` and `integrator`. Parallel writers use isolated worktrees, then an integrator. A verifier directly depends on the artifact owner. Inspect workflow status on recovery; completed nodes are not replayed. Check remote state before retrying external effects. `pstack_worktrees` cleans only owned clean worktrees.
